  "text": "At the quay, Elias stopped beside the mooring posts. The boat beyond the markers was coming in slowly, its sail slackening as it entered the harbor.

“My brother knew the merchant’s boat,” he said. “He could tell when it had come in heavy, even if they unloaded it before dawn.”

Ada looked back toward the square. The shouting had faded, but people were still waiting outside the constable’s office. “Did the harbor master say where your brother went?”

Elias shook his head. He held the list so tightly that its edges bent. “He says my brother took a skiff out to meet them. He says he never saw him come back.”

Mara watched the boat glide past the reef. For months, every account of that night had ended at the same place: Elias’s brother leaving shore alone. Now there were other men in the story, and one of them was on his way to town.

A bell rang from the customs shed. The boat’s crew lowered the sail, and Mara recognized the merchant standing near the bow. He saw the three of them on the quay. For a moment he did not move. Then he spoke to the man at the tiller.

The boat turned away from its usual berth.

“He knows,” Ada said.

Elias started down the quay, but Mara caught his sleeve. Across the harbor, the constable and two officers were already hurrying toward the customs shed. Elias saw them too. He stopped, smoothed the list against his palm, and waited as the boat came in."
